species.name: Awakened Undead
species.description:
You are the skeletal remains of what once was a living creature; you are both the power that animates these remains and bound to the remains themselves. The source of your second life varies—perhaps risen as a mindless undead by a necromancer before you eventually awakened sentience, perhaps a fey spirit that inhabited the bones and got stuck, or perhaps a fiendish creature bound to this form to walk the material plane. Your new life is as fragile as any mortal, and you can die as they do.

This is a unique and flexible species where your exact nature depends on the Remains and Animating Force you select, presenting unique traits and challenges, including some large conveniences and inconveniences, particularly around healing. This species is always subject to your GM's approval: being undead is not a normal player experience, and if your nature is revealed, most creatures will find you either terrifying or a threat to be destroyed.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: As an undead, you have increased resilience. Your Constitution score and one other ability score of choice increase by 1. You gain one additional ability score increase from the type of Remains selected in your subrace choice.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Awakened undead are effectively ageless. Their age can be measured from when they have awakened, but they do not change with age beyond their lived experience from that point.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: While typical undead are nearly universally evil due to the negative energy that animates them, there are other sources of undead animation that run a broader range of possibilities. Regardless of your animating force, what differentiates an Awakened Undead is awareness and control, and as such they can freely choose their alignment. Some will still choose evil, but others find a new path upon awakening.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Undead are typically animated from Medium sized humanoid corpses, and have sizes based on the creature they once were. Your size is Medium unless otherwise specified by your Remains type.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: Due to the unique nature of your sight, you can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: you can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common.

traits.name: Undead Nature
traits.description:
Your creature type is undead, rather than humanoid. As a result of being undead, you have the following benefits:

  • You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
  • You are immune to disease.
  • You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.
You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.
You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

traits.name: Magical Vitality
traits.description:
As you are powered by magic, your vitality can be restored by magical power. Any creature (including you) with access to spell slots can expend a spell slot as an action with a range of touch to restore 1d8 + their spellcasting modifier hit points, donating their magical power to your vitality. The amount restored increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1st. Whenever you are healed in this fashion, you can expend Hit Dice (rolling them as normal) equal to the spell slot level used to regain additional hit points.

Additionally, you can be returned to life with the animate dead spell, which has the effects of revivify when cast targeting only you.

traits.name: Reassembly
traits.description: Your body can be assembled if pieces are broken off. A lost limb can be reattached over a short rest while spending 1 or more Hit Dice as long as the limb is in your possession, and your corpse counts as intact if all pieces of it can be found and assembled for when using animate dead to recreate revivify on you.

traits.name: Turn Resistance
traits.description: Due to your awakened nature, you have advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: you have advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns undead
mechanics.conditionNote: against any effect that turns undead

traits.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
traits.description:
As a magically alive force, you are weakened while in the area of an antimagic field. At the start of each turn you spend in it, you must make a DC 10 Charisma saving throw. On failure, you have disadvantage on all attack rolls and ability checks, and your speed is halved. If you fail by 5 or more, you are stunned until the end of your turn.

If you are the target of dispel magic, you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against the caster's spell save DC (even if the caster is an allied creature). On failure, you are stunned until the end of your next turn.

traits.name: Remains
traits.description: Awakened Undead are extremely varied by their nature, and consequently create their subrace in a unique way by selecting two values: their Remains, and their Animating Force. Your Remains indicates what sort of corpse you are animating. Your selection of Remains gives you an ability score increase (listed below) and a feature.

options.name: Human
options.description:
Ability Score: Any.

Universal Parts. You can often find useful spares laying about, and your parts are easier to repair in general. When you complete a long rest, you regain an additional Hit Die. The number of Hit Dice you regain increases when your proficiency bonus does.

options.name: Elf
options.description:
Ability Score: Dexterity.

Mystic Bones. You have advantage on Charisma saving throws for Antimagic Susceptibility, and you cannot be put to sleep by magical means.

options.name: Dwarf
options.description:
Ability Score: Constitution.

Sturdy Bones. Your bones are particularly sturdy. Your speed becomes 25 feet. Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.

options.name: Minotaur
options.description:
Ability Score: Strength.

Ramming Horns. Your horns are natural melee weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

options.name: Beast
options.description:
Ability Score: Strength or Constitution.

Bestial Configuration. Inconveniently, you don't have hands. You cannot do anything that requires hands (such as holding weapons or casting spells with somatic components), but you can grapple a single target with your mouth. Your movement speed becomes 35 feet, and you gain natural weapons in the form of fangs that deal 1d10 + your Strength modifier piercing damage, and claws that deal 1d6 + your Strength modifier slashing damage. Your claws have the Light property; you are considered to be holding them for the purpose of using them as weapons.

options.name: Catfolk
options.description:
Ability Score: Dexterity.

Climbing Configured. Your remains are well configured for climbing, being light and with built-in claws. You gain a climbing speed of 30 feet.

options.name: Angelic
options.description:
Ability Score: Charisma.

Relic Bones. Your bones have a lingering holy aura. You are immune to effects that turn undead and have resistance to radiant damage.

options.name: Kobold
options.description:
Ability Score: Dexterity.

Scurrying Frame. Your size becomes Small, and you can move through other creatures' spaces as if you were one size smaller (Tiny) but cannot end your turn inside their space unless you otherwise could.

options.name: Turtlefolk
options.description:
Ability Score: Constitution.

Bone Shell. Your remains have a sturdy bone shell that can be used to deflect attacks. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 17. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

options.name: Centaur
options.description:
Ability Score: Strength.

Galloping Frame. Your movement speed becomes 35 feet, but any climb that requires hands and feet is especially difficult for you because of your equine legs. When you make such a climb, each foot of movement costs you 4 extra feet, instead of the normal 1 extra foot.

traits.name: Animating Force
traits.description: Your Animating Force dictates what sort of force is driving your animation. Your Animating Force gives a language known as well as a feature. If the language is listed as "matching remains" it means the language of the type of corpse you are animating spoke in life (for example, for an elf corpse, Elvish).

options.name: Necromancy
options.description:
Language: Matching Remains.

Emotional Void. You are animated by a thread of negative energy that has somehow gained greater awareness. You still feel the innate urge to destroy all life, and can control and channel that urge. As a bonus action, you can unleash your normal undead nature for 1 minute. You become immune to the charmed and frightened conditions, but lose your Turn Resistance feature. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

options.name: Wandering Spirit
options.description:
Language: Any.

Spirit Soaring. You're loosely bound to this shell and capable of soaring free of it. As an action, you can cast gaseous form, but rather than transforming you leave your body behind, incapacitated, and when the spell ends you return to your body's location. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

characteristics.label: gaseous form, but rather than transforming you leave your body behind, incapacitated, when the

options.name: Returned Spirit
options.description:
Language: Matching Remains.

Remembrance. You've come back for your own bones... or at least you think you have. You retain some of the skills you had in life. You can select one of the following: proficiency in a simple or martial weapon of your choice, or proficiency in two skills or tools of your choice. You additionally gain proficiency in one artisan's tool or language of your choice.

options.name: Fey Energy
options.description:
You know Sylvan.

Fey Spirit. Sometimes a fey spirit finds itself inhabiting a pile of bones, often not entirely aware of who, what, or why, as is their way. Your creature type is both Fey and Undead. You have access to additional fey magic, and cast faerie fire and speak with animals each once without expending a spell slot, regaining the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

characteristics.label: faerie fire, speak with animals each (no slot or psi cost)

options.name: Infernal Energy
options.description:
You know Infernal.

Flaming Skeleton. You glow with an inner flame. As a bonus action, you can burst alight, becoming a flaming skeleton for 1 minute. For the duration, you have resistance to fire damage and any other creature that starts their turn within 5 feet of you takes 1d4 fire damage. While this effect is active, once per turn when you hit a creature within 5 feet of you with an attack or deal fire damage, you can add bonus damage to that damage roll equal to your proficiency bonus (affecting one target of the damage roll). Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

options.name: Blight Growth
options.description:
Language: None.

Blightborn. Uniquely your animating force is a physical (though still magical) phenomenon; twisting vines growing through your remains. Your creature type is both Plant and Undead, and you can leverage your vines to constrict your enemies. You can grapple a number of creatures equal to your Constitution modifier without using your hands.

species.name: Ironwrought
species.description: While most constructs are not truly self-aware, an Ironwrought is a special case of a construct that has attained a full degree of self-awareness—sometimes in a more rudimentary way, sometimes as self-aware as any human. The origins of Ironwrought are many and varied. They can be the artisanal masterpiece of a Golemsmith, or perhaps a relic of a mass production of an ancient lost civilization. Were they made with sapience in mind, or did they gain it later? Were they made for labor or war? Many Ironwrought will dwell on these questions, but just as many simply move on, finding their purpose in life as any of their more fleshy counterparts might.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and one other ability score of your choice increases by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Constructs do not age physically, though their mental abilities may change greatly through their life as they process new information and experiences.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Ironwrought tend to be inclined toward Lawful Neutral, following an internal logic and purpose, but player Ironwrought have gained full sapience, and can make their own decisions. Some opt to rebel entirely against their nature, acting in unpredictable chaotic patterns like any mortals.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Living Construct
traits.description: You are immune to disease. You do not need to eat, drink, or breathe. You do not need sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice (usually the language of your creator if they spoke a language other than Common).

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice

traits.name: Power Down
traits.description: You do not need to sleep. When you take a long rest, you must spend at least 4 hours during a long rest in a motionless lower power state. While in this state, you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, but remain aware of your surroundings.

traits.name: Construct
traits.description: Your type is construct.

traits.name: Arcane Life
traits.description: You can absorb certain types of healing magic, allowing you to recover hit points from magical effects that do not otherwise affect constructs (such as the cure wounds spell).

traits.name: Modular Design
traits.description: You can select two of the following specialized traits representing the functionality built into your chassis.

options.name: Integrated Armor
options.description: You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

options.name: Integrated Weapon
options.description: You have a simple or martial weapon of your choice built into your frame. You gain proficiency with this weapon. This doesn't remove the need for ammunition for weapons that have the ammunition property. This weapon is typically integrated into your limbs, and requires hands to use as normal.

options.name: Language Module
options.description: You learn one additional language, and can cast comprehend languages without consuming a spell slot. Once you cast this spell, you can't cast it again until you finish a long rest. You can cast this spell using spell slots.

options.name: Natural Armor
options.description: You have built-in armor, giving you a base AC of 16 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can use a shield and apply the shield's bonus as normal.

options.name: Night Mode
options.description: You have darkvision within 60 feet. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

options.name: Rapid Movement
options.description: Your base walking speed increases by 5 feet.

options.name: Redundant Logic
options.description: You process all inputs twice to ensure they are logical. You have advantage on saving throws against becoming frightened or charmed.

options.name: Specialized Skill
options.description: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

options.name: Specialized Tool
options.description: You gain one tool built into your frame. You gain proficiency with this tool.

options.name: Terrain Adaptation
options.description: You gain a climbing or swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

traits.name: Chassis Configuration
traits.description: Ironwrought come in many shapes and sizes. Select one of the following configurations of your chassis.

options.name: Humanoid
options.description:
Your shape is roughly that of a bipedal humanoid.

Adaptable Design. You can make one additional selection from your Modular Design trait.

options.name: Quadrupedal
options.description:
Your shape has four legs and no hands.

Quadrupedal. You do not have hands. You can hold one object or grapple one thing using your mouth, but can't speak when you do so, and any weapons held in this way are wielded with disadvantage. You can perform the somatic components of spells with one of your legs, however doing so requires 15 feet of your movement.

Natural Weapons. You gain a selection of natural weapons. You are considered to be holding natural weapons for the purposes of abilities that require you to hold a weapon (this doesn't confer disadvantage to them). Select two of the following: Metal Chompers (metal fangs; on hit, deal 1d10 piercing damage), Razor Claws (two sets of razor claws integrated into your front limbs; on hit, deal 1d6 slashing damage and have the light property), or Bladed Tail (a lashing bladed tail; on hit, deals 1d4 slashing damage and has the reach property).

Barding. You can only wear armor specially adapted to your unique shape. This custom armor has the same price as normal armor, but may be harder to find or more expensive when custom ordered.

traits.name: Variant Large Constructs (Optional)
traits.description:
At the discretion of your GM, a quadrupedal Ironwrought construct can be Large sized. It gains the following traits:

Large Natural Weapons. The damage dice of your natural weapons increases by one size (from a d10 to a d12 or from a d6 to a d8). Your natural weapons without the light property gain the heavy property.

Bulwark. You count as three-quarters cover for allied creatures when you would normally count as half cover.

Barding. You can't wear armor designed for normal-sized creatures. Your armor has to be designed for Large-sized creatures of your form, and generally costs four times the normal cost of armor.

species.name: Farling
species.description: Farlings are a species that comes from beyond the material plane, though few are certain where. While humanoid in shape, they are immediately distinguished from mortal races. They have a slender build, large eyes, and tendrils in place of hair. Their strange nature and inherent psionic abilities make them easily feared, but they tend to be far more friendly to mortal races than most of that which comes from the beyond. Farlings are exceedingly adept at picking up social cues and cultural norms, and despite their strange appearance can easily fit into a tolerant society, but often maintain exceedingly strange senses of humor and behavior, fully aware of its oddity.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Intelligence score, Wisdom score, and Charisma score all increase by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: A Farling ages by absorbing memories. Each time they permanently absorb a memory, they age roughly one day. A young Farling can absorb dozens of memories a day, aging rapidly. Once reaching adulthood (a process that often only takes a decade), the rate at which they can absorb memories begins to slow, and they become more selective, aging far slower.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Farlings show little consistency in alignment, and are shaped by their circumstances and background. Their curious and impulsive nature often leads younger members of the race to exhibit chaotic tendencies.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Most Farlings stand between 5 and 6 feet tall, with a slighter build than humans. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Aberration
traits.description: Your creature type is Aberration, rather than humanoid.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet. You have a swimming speed of 20 feet.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You have a swimming speed of 20 feet.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You have a swimming speed of 20 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common, Deep Speech, and one extra language of your choice.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common, Deep Speech, and one extra language of your choice.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You can speak, read, and write Common, Deep Speech, and one extra language of your choice.

traits.name: Adaptive Intuition
traits.description: You gain proficiency in Insight, and have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to determine social cues or cultural customs.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to determine social cues or cultural customs
mechanics.conditionNote: to determine social cues or cultural customs

traits.name: Psionic Mind
traits.description: You gain the Telepathy Discipline of the psion, though you can't use the Alternate Effects unless you gain this Discipline from another source. If you gain this Discipline from another source, you gain 1 additional psi point instead. References the psion's Telepathy Discipline and psi point pool, defined in the Psion class chapter.

traits.name: Crystalized Memory
traits.description: When you learn or experience something, you can fix that memory, making it a permanent memory you can always remember with crystal clarity. This memory can be anything that occurs within a 1 hour span (it can be as short as a fleeting sensation, or as long as 1 hour of events). Once you do this, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Absorbing these memories is how a Farling ages, and you age one day for each memory you absorb in this way. You can absorb a memory from a willing creature via your telepathy in this way.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: Once you do this, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

traits.name: Broad Horizons
traits.description: You have resistance to psychic damage. Once per day, if you take psychic damage from a critical hit, you can choose to absorb that damage as a memory, taking no damage.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You have resistance to psychic damage.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You have resistance to psychic damage.

traits.name: Skill Absorption
traits.description: Your rapid ability to learn new skills grants you proficiency in one artisan tool and one skill of your choice. At your GM's discretion, if your game allows for the training in tools and skills, you may gain proficiency in them twice as fast using your Crystalized Memory feature daily.

proficiency in one artisan tool and one skill of your choice

traits.name: Alien Mind (Optional Variant)
traits.description: At the discretion of your GM, this feature can be added in place of Skill Absorption. When you gain the Spellcasting or Psionics ability from any class or feature, you can change the associated ability score to your choice of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Any time that class references the previous spellcasting ability, you can replace it with your selected score (for example, if you are playing a Psion and change its associated ability score to Charisma, Empowered Psionics would add Charisma instead of Intelligence).

species.name: Augmented
species.description:
The augmented are creatures that have replaced parts of the body with mechanical and magical parts—some sort of arcane cyborg. The origin of these parts is many and varied, as is their nature: anything from living magic to mechanical means is possible, based on the setting and character. Almost all augmented are intentionally created—not always by the intentions of the individual, but almost always by the intention of someone. Many are created for war, some as bizarre experiments, some to restore missing pieces.

This is a template placed over an existing race option, not a standalone species. Though an augmented creature superficially inherits the appearance of its base race, all mechanical benefits of that race are replaced by the properties below. You still qualify for any feat or other requirement that applies to the base selected race.

traits.name: Modified Origin
traits.description: Select an existing race option. You gain the creature type, size, and languages of that race.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 1, and one ability score of your choice increases by 1.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: An augmented creature can be any alignment, but has an inclination toward lawful alignments.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Inherited Abilities
traits.description: You can keep the following elements of that race: any skill proficiencies you gained from it and any climbing, flying, or swimming speed you gained from it. Alternatively, you can forgo this to select one additional option from Augmented Abilities.

traits.name: Augmented Abilities
traits.description: On top of your inherited abilities, you have been augmented with one of the following, granting you special new abilities.

options.name: Arcane Arm
options.description: Your arm is replaced by a mechanical or magical replacement. Your Strength score increases by 1, and it can serve as a natural weapon. It deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage on hit, and counts as a simple weapon with the light property.

options.name: Arcane Eye
options.description: Your eye (one or both) are replaced by mechanical or magical replacements. You have darkvision within 120 feet. You can see in dim light within 120 feet of you as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You discern colors in that darkness as shades of gray, and gain proficiency in the Perception skill. You can cast the detect magic spell, and once you reach 5th level, the see invisibility spell with this eye. Casting them in this way requires no material components. Once you cast either of these spells with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have.

options.name: Arcane Heart
options.description: Your heart (or equivalent organ) is replaced by a mechanical or magical replacement. Your Constitution score increases by 1, and whenever you roll Hit Dice, you gain temporary hit points equal to the number of Hit Dice expended.

options.name: Arcane Mind
options.description: Your mind is enhanced by mechanical or magical minds. Your Intelligence score increases by 1, and you gain advantage on any Intelligence check to recall information you've seen before, solve mathematical equations, detect patterns, or break ciphers and codes.

species.name: Warped
species.description:
The warped are members of races that have been deeply influenced by the powers from beyond, twisting their mind and body with mysterious power that has left them fundamentally changed. Most often this comes from long exposure, sometimes only manifesting in creatures born under its influence, but there are those that have been warped later in life through more direct interactions with the creatures that lurk beyond the veil of sanity. Many of the warped fall to madness, unable to escape the whispering voices and strange visions, but those that become adventurers have managed to learn to live with their condition, and consequently have minds of steel.

This is a template placed over an existing race option, not a standalone species. Though a warped creature superficially inherits the appearance of its base race, all mechanical benefits of that race are replaced by the properties below.

traits.name: Warped Origin
traits.description: Select an existing race option. You gain the creature type, size, and languages of that race.

traits.name: Whispers of Madness
traits.description: You have learned to understand the whispering voices you hear. You learn Deep Speech.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 1, and your Intelligence score increases by 2.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: A warped creature can be any alignment, but has an inclination toward chaotic alignments.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Inured of Madness
traits.description: Things that cause madness in others seem relatively benign to you. You have resistance to psychic damage. You automatically pass any saves against madness.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You have resistance to psychic damage.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You have resistance to psychic damage.

traits.name: Inner Voice
traits.description: You have an inner voice that doesn't belong to you, frequently muttering nonsense, but occasionally offering useful advice, letting you add 1d6 to any ability check you make. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses at the end of a long rest.

mechanics.sourcePhrase: You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses at the end of a long rest.

importModifierMeta.matchedPhrase: You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses at the end of a long rest.

traits.name: Warped Gift
traits.description: Your condition grants you one special trait. Some may view it as a curse or burden, but you've adapted to using it to your advantage. Select one of the following options.

options.name: Warped Eyes
options.description: You see the world in a different way. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks against living creatures, and disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks against non-living things (such as traps or details in your environment).

options.name: Warped Limb
options.description: One of your limbs is abnormally long and flexible. Any weapon wielded in that hand gains the reach property.

options.name: Warped Mind
options.description: Your mind is a foreign and alien place compared to other humanoids. You are immune to magic that allows other creatures to read your thoughts, determine whether you are lying, know your alignment, or know your creature type. Creatures can telepathically communicate with you only if you allow it.

options.name: Warped Skin
options.description: Your skin is a rough mottled hide. You have resistance to acid damage.

options.name: Warped Form
options.description: Your body is more malleable and flexible than a normal humanoid. You can move through spaces for smaller creatures without squeezing, and when you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

feats.name: Modified Remains
feats.description:
You've found your remains to be somewhat... customizable. After all, what's the harm in swapping out a few parts here and there? You gain the following benefits:

  • Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • Skeleton Carving. You gain a natural weapon that deals 2d4 damage (piercing or slashing, your choice) or increase your AC by 1. If you already have a natural weapon and select a natural weapon, you can increase the damage of your existing natural weapon by a d2 step instead (from a d6 to a d8, for example). If a natural weapon has multiple damage dice, increase only one this way.

feats.name: Twice Awakened
feats.description:
You've mastered a second power of Awakening, gaining control of a greater set of powers over your condition. This can be from infusing yourself with energy of that source, or simply learning to imitate the powers natural to that source (for example, a returned spirit may find themselves mastering the powers of a Wandering Spirit after getting used to the condition). You gain the following benefits:

  • Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • Secondary Force. Select an additional option from the Animating Force table, gaining its features.

feats.name: Refined Control
feats.description:
You gain more granular control over your body, even when it is not all attached, allowing it to take advantage of its unnatural properties. You gain the following benefits:

  • Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • Removable Parts. You can remove a limb and continue to control it. It gains the statistics of a Crawling Claw, but has a blindsight of 5 × your proficiency bonus instead of 30 feet. This crawling claw gains all the abilities of a familiar as per the find familiar spell. You lose use of the limb for anything else while it is not attached. If it is destroyed, you can attach a new limb over the course of a long rest.
  • Dullahan. Being beheaded (for example, by a vorpal sword) is no longer fatal to you, though your body cannot move more than 120 feet from your head.
